name: FL-20
label: Safe D

key_factors: Wasserman Schultz's large financial advantage ($1.9M cash vs. $41K)
Incumbent running in a seat Democrats hold
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~95%
model.rationale: The district's D+20 partisan lean, an incumbent Democrat with a massive fundraising edge, and markets pricing a Democratic win near 95% all point the same way; the Republican has raised only about $64,000. The forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based expectation of a roughly 25-point Democratic margin.
model.watch: A surprise scandal, major outside spending for Andersen, or an unusually strong Republican national environment could narrow the margin, though a flip remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Incumbent Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D) is running.

overview:
Debbie Wasserman Schultz, a longtime incumbent, is heavily favored to hold this South Florida seat after Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick's resignation. The district carries a D+20 partisan lean, and the incumbent has raised over $3.3 million with $1.9 million still on hand. Republican Brent Andersen has raised under $65,000, leaving him little capacity to compete in an expensive Miami-area media market.

Prediction markets put the Democratic win probability around 95%, and no independent polls or expert ratings contradict that picture. An independent candidate in the field is unlikely to alter the outcome materially. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
